subject: environmental-science

moments.title: Lotka-Volterra equations
moments.body: Independently, Lotka (1925, 'Elements of Physical Biology') and Volterra (1926, observing Adriatic fish stocks) derive coupled differential equations for predator-prey dynamics. The equations produce oscillating populations — observed in lynx-hare data from the Hudson's Bay Company over 80+ years. Verhulst's earlier logistic equation (1838) for single populations had been forgotten and rediscovered.
moments.takeaway: Mathematical ecology emerged from two independent insights and was confirmed by century-old fur trapping records.

now.title: Population dynamics today
now.body: Lotka-Volterra is a teaching foundation but practical models are far more complex (age structure, stochasticity, spatial dynamics, climate forcing). Fishery management uses sophisticated stock-assessment models; many large fisheries have collapsed despite them. North Atlantic cod (1992 collapse) remains a cautionary case.
now.open_questions: Can ecosystem-based management replace single-species fishery models? Multi-species interactions are observable but hard to predict.

reflection: Volterra's daughter married a marine biologist whose Adriatic fish data prompted the modelling. Family conversations occasionally launch sub-fields.
